Motivation, implementation and evidence scope
Question and scope

Can simple facial de-identification preserve remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) while reducing identity-related similarity? This CPU portfolio provides a classical baseline, controlled experiments and a descriptive embedding demonstration. It is not a reproduction of the supervisors' learned method, clinical validation or proven anonymity. Work was developed with AI assistance; the applicant must personally review and understand the implementation.
Inputs and privacy

A 30-second cartoon injects 72 BPM for engineering checks. A private facial recording has sparse Garmin processed HR, not raw PPG. Three officially research-shared UBFC Dataset 2 participants supply facial video and contact PPG. Subject 1 was previously inspected; subjects 3/4 were selected before their outcomes. Their initial video downloads were quota-blocked, then the user supplied the prescribed files locally. Both new recordings ran under strict Haar/LK and a separate automatic YuNet variant. Inputs, locations, tracking, model caches and previews remain local/ignored. No raw data, face images or embedding vectors are published/uploaded.
CPU pipeline

OpenCV face geometry defines approximate forehead and cheek patches. Equal-weight patch RGB means enter independent POS or simplified CHROM, followed by third-order zero-phase 0.7-3 Hz filtering, standardization and 2-second edge trim. HR is the dominant Welch peak (10-second segments, 4096 FFT points). Overlapping 30-second windows advance 15 seconds. Zero padding does not add physiological resolution; zero-phase processing is offline. Original geometry is reused across variants, so transformed-only detection is not assumed to work. Blur sigma / face size is 0.10, pixelation grid is 8x8, and black masking is a negative control.
Reproducibility and upstream comparisons

macOS arm 64, Anaconda Python 3.13.5; scientific dependencies and settings are recorded. pyVHR-cpu 1.0.2 unmodified CPU methods ran through an isolated loader, not the full video Pipeline. POS matched local aggregate HR and correlated about 0.99997 on private traces. rPPG-Toolbox classical POS ran at commit b7500b848f84ad7f86e277b4612563b69f4f88f9 with explicit NumPy 2 np.mat compatibility; waveform correlations were about 0.974-0.977. Its internal filters differ. No neural training, CUDA, CSC job or full dataset-loader benchmark ran.
Verification and literature

43 project tests pass, including signal recovery, failures, timestamps, duplicate handling, target filtering and embedding validity. Synthetic recovery is 72.07 BPM versus 72 injected; this is not human accuracy. Configurations, source/model hashes, logs and separate result folders preserve experiment scope. Savic and Zhao [1] motivate joint utility/privacy evaluation; Wei et al. [2] provide wider privacy context. PhysFormer [3] and Contrast-Phys+ [4] motivate future learned/label-efficient work. Accessible primary abstracts/records and author README were consulted; full-text critical reading remains incomplete.
Expanded tests, failures and reference uncertainty
Sampling and fixed settings

Subject 1 is a development case: strict Haar/LK fails on a shirt false-positive, a manual-region fallback completes, and a later YuNet variant detects all 1547 frames. The newly supplied subjects 3/4 were not used to adjust the signal or quality rules. Both automatic detector conditions complete without manual regions. Subject 3 contributes two overlapping 30-second windows; subject 4 contributes one. This is only three distinct new intervals from two people, not 18 independent observations when six method/variant combinations are applied. Settings and model versions were fixed before new outcomes.
Actual expanded HR results

Against the fixed contact-PPG spectral reference, YuNet POS MAE (original/blur/pixelation) is 1.95/8.66/8.44 BPM on subject 3 and 0.43/0.43/0.43 on subject 4. YuNet CHROM is 1.08/0.87/7.14 on subject 3 and 0.43/0.43/0.43 on subject 4. Original Haar/LK on subject 3 gives POS 37.66/25.97/15.37 and CHROM 0.00/0.43/14.50 BPM; on subject 4 POS is 0.43/0.43/0.43 and CHROM 0.87/0.43/0.43. Every condition is retained; detector choice is not selected per person for favourable error. Black-mask signals are invalid, not zero-error successes. A matching spectral bin does not mean perfect accuracy.
The reference is not unquestionable truth

Subject3 contact PPG has competing components. Welch selects 87.43/84.84 BPM, with next peaks 100.85/104.31. A post-hoc audit finds median detected pulse-interval HR 98.49 across 12 fixed filter/polarity/prominence settings; span-count summaries are 94.28-96.17 and device HR 100.95/104.56. Native-time Lomb-Scargle strongest peaks are 101.40/89.82. Duration endpoints differ by less than 0.15 s across recordings, without a gross global scale mismatch. These methods estimate different summaries and processing choices matter; none is independently adjudicated truth. All settings are retained, baselines unchanged. Errors and warning labels remain conditional on the original spectral-reference estimate, not clinical accuracy. See docs/REFERENCE_AUDIT.md.
Quality rule: both missed events and false alarms

The post-hoc rule warns for strongest/distinct-competitor ratio below 1.2 or a dominant peak near the band edge. This caught the earlier private POS peak switch (64.6 to 44.8 BPM), but does not guarantee correct HR. For new non-mask assessments, error >5 BPM vs the fixed reference gives Haar TP 4/FP 5/FN 3/TN 6 and YuNet TP 2/FP 6/FN 1/TN 9. There are 18 correlated assessments per detector, sharing only three temporal intervals; six share the same ambiguous contact-reference interval. These are descriptive counts, not validated classifier performance. No threshold was changed after these results.
Interpretation and supporting preservation experiments

Results vary substantially across people, detector geometry and transformations. The earlier subject 1 low errors are not representative of all recordings. Reference uncertainty prevents treating every deviation as genuine physiological failure. Private strength sweeps show waveform correlation declining with more blur/pixelation; stable aggregate HR can conceal window failures. Original geometry is reused for transformed variants, and signed zero-lag correlation may preserve shared artifacts. Spectral-concentration ratio is a surrogate, not GT SNR. Full participant/window tables and raw failure logs are preserved in the experiment folders and docs/EXPANDED_VALIDATION.md.
Three-identity embedding experiment and honest claims
Model and temporal split

Official OpenCV Zoo YuNet 2023mar (MIT) and SFace 2021dec (Apache 2.0) run on CPU at pinned revision 48b10fa505aeb51fbd127fc60a5c660040e823b7 with hashes. Original frames at 5/10/15 s of subjects 1/3/4 form three normalized 128-dimensional enrollment templates. Probes at 30/35/40 s give nine images, each compared with its genuine template and two impostors. Enrollment/probes use different frames but the SAME capture session per person. All required enrollment and original-probe detections succeeded. No new private identities, real-world names or recognition thresholds are inferred.
Measured similarities and detection failures

Mean genuine cosine is 0.983510 original, 0.125149 blur, 0.201605 pixelation and 0.146126 mask. Unique own-template rank 1 matches are 9/9, 6/9, 8/9 and 6/9 respectively. Genuine must strictly exceed both impostor scores; ties are not successes. Closed-set ranking forces a choice among only three templates even when scores are low; it is not calibrated verification. Original landmarks align transformed probes, an explicit assistance condition. Separate re-detection succeeds 9/9 on original and 0/9 on transformed probes; missing end-to-end similarities are undefined, not zero or anonymity. Images/embedding vectors are not saved.
Privacy interpretation

Lower cosine did not consistently remove own-template ranking. Even the masked control yields 6/9 matches, highlighting possible residual context/geometry and model/gallery bias; this is not proof of recovering facial biometrics through a mask. The cause is unresolved. Three correlated probes per identity and two impostors cannot establish anonymity or general re-identification performance. Independent-session enrollment, larger cohorts and cross-model tests are needed. Assisted identity geometry differs from the YuNet physiological experiment; do not merge them into a matched privacy/utility frontier.
Strongest current claim and next work

The portfolio provides a reproducible CPU baseline with controlled preservation experiments, three public participants, two automatic detector conditions, upstream comparisons, descriptive quality warnings and a small embedding cohort. It records poor outcomes and reference uncertainty rather than claiming universal sub-1-BPM errors. Strongest claim: practical implementation and evaluation with explicit limits, not anonymous video or clinical validation. Next: reference adjudication, challenging independent data, independent identity sessions, full-text critical reading and interview rehearsal. Publication requires explicit permission; CSC remains optional.
